q-108162.name: Question 1
q-108162.problem:
Given that the random variable $X∼{χ}^{2}(8),$ calculate $P(X<6).$ Round your final answer to four decimal places.

*Hint: You may wish to make use of the following result:*

$$
{\int }_{0}^{6}{x}^{3}{e}^{-x/2}\,\text{d}x≈33.86574
$$

*The probability density function ${χ}^{2}(k)$ is given by*

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{{2}^{k/2}Γ(\frac{k}{2})}{x}^{k/2-1}{e}^{-x/2}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
q-108162.worked_solution:
A chi-square random variable $X∼{χ}^{2}(k)$ with $k$ degrees of freedom has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{{2}^{k/2}Γ(\frac{k}{2})}{x}^{k/2-1}{e}^{-x/2}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that $X∼{χ}^{2}(8).$ So, $X$ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{16Γ(4)}{x}^{3}{e}^{-x/2}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Recalling that $Γ(n)=(n-1)!$ for any natural number $n\ge 1,$ we have

$$
Γ(4)=3!=6.
$$

So, the probability distribution becomes

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{96}{x}^{3}{e}^{-x/2}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate $P(X<6)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<6) & ={\int }_{0}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{6}\frac{1}{96}{x}^{3}{e}^{-x/2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{96}{\int }_{0}^{6}{x}^{3}{e}^{-x/2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ≈\frac{1}{96}\cdot 33.86574 \\  & ≈0.3528\end{aligned}
$$

q-108186.problem:
Given that $X∼{χ}^{2}(8),$ what is $P(X<6)$ expressed as an integral?

*Hint: The probability density function ${χ}^{2}(k)$ is given by*

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{{2}^{k/2}Γ(\frac{k}{2})}{x}^{k/2-1}{e}^{-x/2}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}

q-108186.html:
Question 2
?

Given that X∼χ2(8), what is P(X<6) expressed as an integral?

Hint: The probability density function χ2(k) is given by

f(x)={12k/2Γ(k2)xk/2−1e−x/2,x≥00,otherwise.

a
196∫06x6e−x/2dx
b
196∫06x3e−x/2dx
c
18∫06x2e−x/2dx
d
116∫06x4e−x/2dx
e
116∫06x3e−x/2dx
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

A chi-square random variable X∼χ2(k) with k degrees of freedom has the following probability density function:

f(x)={12k/2Γ(k2)xk/2−1e−x/2,x≥00,otherwise

We're given that X∼χ2(8). So, X has the following probability density function:

f(x)={116Γ(4)x3e−x/2,x≥00,otherwise

Recalling that Γ(n)=(n−1)! for any natural number n≥1, we have

Γ(4)=3!=6.

So, the probability distribution becomes

f(x)={196x3e−x/2,x≥00,otherwise.

Finally, we calculate P(X<6) as follows:

P(X<6)=∫06f(x)dx=∫06196x3e−x/2dx=196∫06x3e−x/2dx

q-108300.name: Question 5
q-108300.worked_solution:
The table shows probabilities in the form $P(X>x).$ So first, we express the desired probability in this form:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>x) & =1-P(X\le x) \\  & =1-0.025 \\  & =0.975\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $X∼{χ}^{2}(4),$ we focus on the row of the table that corresponds to $k=4.$

| $k∖p$ | $0.995$ | $0.990$ | $0.975$ | $0.950$ | $0.900$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $4$ | $\,0.207\,$ | $\,0.297\,$ | $\,0.484\,$ | $\,0.711\,$ | $\,1.064\,$ |

From this row, we see that

$$
P(X>0.484)=0.975.
$$

Therefore, our answer is $x=0.484.$
